papers.title: In situ structure of the human ciliary transition zone links linker defects to primary ciliary dyskinesia.
papers.summary: Using in situ cryo-electron tomography of human multiciliated epithelial cells, researchers resolved the ciliary transition zone at subnanometer resolution, identifying nine constituent proteins. ECT2L and DZANK1 form the major linkers between doublet microtubules; loss-of-function variants in either gene cause primary ciliary dyskinesia, disrupting transition zone architecture, ciliary tips, and mucociliary clearance.

papers.title: Glycan recognition by a plant damage-sensing immune receptor.
papers.summary: Pathogens degrade plant cell walls, but how wall-derived damage signals trigger immunity was unclear. Structural analysis of the IGP1 receptor, alone and bound to cellulose-derived cellotriose, reveals leucine-rich repeat-malectin domains preconfigured for ligand recognition and a sugar-binding pocket distinguishing fine glycan differences, making IGP1 a cell wall surveillance receptor linking damage to immune alerting.

papers.title: Noncoding transcription controls the developmental dynamics of long-range gene regulation.
papers.summary: Using live imaging in Drosophila embryos, single-allele visualization shows that sequential transcription of noncoding RNAs from distinct regulatory elements underlies gene activation. Optimal activation requires only moderate enhancer activity; disrupting enhancer-associated ncRNAs causes precocious activation. ncRNAs locally modulate regulatory element activity in cis, shaping long-range interactions and the timing of developmental gene expression.

papers.title: Lean adipocyte oxylipin signaling restrains breast cancer through ferroptosis.
papers.summary: Mammary adipocytes secrete the oxylipin 9s-HODE, which induces ferroptosis in breast cancer cells by disrupting iron homeostasis. Obese mammary tissue produces less 9s-HODE, and restoring it suppresses tumor growth in obese mice. Human mammary 9s-HODE inversely correlates with BMI and inhibits patient-derived organoid growth, suggesting ferroptosis-inducing lipid restoration as therapy.

papers.title: Extensive and differential platinum chemotherapy mutagenesis in livers of children.
papers.summary: Using duplex sequencing (nanoseq) on normal pediatric tissues, researchers showed platinum chemotherapeutics raise mutation burdens in children to adult levels. Liver tissues acquired a tissue-specific platinum mutational signature, and gene-focused sequencing revealed diverse nonsynonymous variants, including potentially leukemogenic ones in blood—providing a plausible mutational link between chemotherapy exposure and late adverse effects in survivors.

papers.title: Unphosphorylated tyrosines mediate PD-1 inhibition of T cell signaling condensate formation.
papers.summary: PD-1's cytoplasmic domain directly inhibits TCR-induced LAT condensate formation in vitro. Contrary to current models, inhibition required unphosphorylated tyrosines in PD-1's inhibitory motifs—phosphorylation eliminated inhibition, and tyrosine-to-tryptophan substitution reconstituted it. Inhibitory receptors may therefore block immune activation primarily through hydrogen bond-donating aromatic residues rather than phosphorylation-dependent mechanisms.

papers.title: Paleogenomics and habitat modeling reveal temperate Eurasian origins of woolly rhinoceroses.
papers.summary: Sequencing 29 mitochondrial and 14 nuclear genomes from Pleistocene woolly rhinoceros specimens and modeling habitats over 500,000 years indicate maternal diversity arose in temperate Eurasia around 460,000-420,000 years ago. A ~170,000-year-old East Asian individual was ancestral to later populations, and the Altai region served as a major climatic refugium for cold-adapted megafauna.

papers.title: Chronic type II interferon promotes tumor growth through mitochondrial RNA-induced type I interferon and prostaglandin synthesis.
papers.summary: Chronic type II interferon promotes tumor growth by releasing double-stranded mitochondrial RNA into the cytoplasm, inducing a type I interferon response that synergizes with IFN-II to increase COX-2-driven prostaglandin E2 synthesis. Eliminating PGE2 production in immunotherapy-resistant melanoma cells restored anti-PD1 responsiveness, identifying a covert mtRNA-IFN-prostaglandin pathway as a therapeutic target.

papers.title: Manipulation of protein translation and stem cell self-renewal by CRISPR activation of rRNA transcription.
papers.summary: TAPIR is a CRISPR-based approach that elevates rRNA levels by activating 47S ribosomal DNA transcription. It increased nucleolar size and protein synthesis, and in neural stem cells enhanced translation, promoting self-renewal and proliferation in vitro and in vivo, while enabling modeling and partial rescue of disease phenotypes—establishing protein synthesis capacity as a stem cell behavior determinant.

papers.title: WDR23 prevents bone loss by promoting autophagic degradation of TRAF6 in osteoclastogenesis.
papers.summary: WDR23/DCAF11 is identified as a novel TRAF6-binding partner and negative feedback regulator of RANKL-induced osteoclastogenesis. Via WD40 domains, WDR23 binds TRAF6 and promotes its autophagy-dependent degradation, attenuating NF-κB and MAPK signaling and osteoclastogenic markers. WDR23-deficient mice show osteoporosis with elevated osteoclast formation and reduced bone mass, highlighting a therapeutic target for bone disorders.

papers.title: SERINC2-mediated phosphatidylserine remodeling activates protrusion-localized AXL signaling to promote brain metastasis.
papers.summary: In invading cancer cells, SERINC2 acts as a scaffold recruiting the ER-plasma membrane phosphatidylserine transporter OSBPL8 to cell protrusions, driving phosphatidylserine accumulation and externalization, protrusion-localized AXL activation, and invasion. SERINC2-dependent extracellular vesicles stimulate autocrine AXL signaling and M2-like microglia polarization, enhancing orthotopic brain tumor growth and revealing a spatial lipid remodeling axis.

papers.title: Genetic variation in glucosamine metabolism contributes to the colonization resistance of Bacteroides to Salmonella.
papers.summary: Comparing Salmonella-resistant Tibetan chickens with susceptible broilers, Bacteroides enrichment—particularly B. salanitronis—was associated with colonization resistance. Bacteroides competitively deplete N-acetyl-D-glucosamine via highly efficient glucosamine-6-phosphate deaminase; residue Ile138 confers the catalytic advantage over Salmonella's enzyme. Supplementation reduced Salmonella colonization, suggesting microbiome-based strategies against enteric pathogens.

papers.title: Zebrafish sox9b+ cells function as intestinal stem cells for epithelial homeostasis and regeneration.
papers.summary: Zebrafish sox9b+ cells in the proliferative zones of intestinal furrows are functional intestinal stem cells: they drive epithelial turnover during homeostasis, differentiate into nearly all epithelial lineages, and supply neogenic epithelium after injury. Sox9b is essential for intestinal stemness, providing a comparative model for stem cell function in intestines lacking mammalian-type crypts.

papers.title: Newly identified human aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase complex interacting multifunctional protein 2 (AIMP2) loss-of-function mutations cause neurodevelopmental defects linked to cell death in a zebrafish model.
papers.summary: AIMP2, a component of the aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase multisynthetase complex, was characterized in two patients with severe neurodevelopmental disorders. Patient fibroblasts showed reduced AIMP2 protein, attenuated protein synthesis, and dysregulated MARS1; CRISPR disruption in zebrafish caused brain cell death and atrophy. Anticodon-engineered suppressor tRNAs dramatically increased expression from disease-associated nonsense variants, suggesting a therapy avenue.

papers.title: Trichomonas vaginalis cathepsin D-like aspartic proteinase (Tv-CatD) is regulated by iron at different levels.
papers.journal: Biometals : an international journal on the role of metal ions in biology, biochemistry, and medicine
papers.summary: In Trichomonas vaginalis, iron regulates the cathepsin D-like proteinase Tv-CatD post-transcriptionally and post-translationally: mRNA was unchanged, but high iron increased protein abundance ~2.6-fold and promoted vesicle-mediated surface mobilization and secretion, while Fe2+ directly inhibited enzymatic activity, with secreted activity ~4.7-fold lower under high iron. Iron thus differentially modulates this virulence-associated protease.

papers.title: Chromosome-scale genome assembly and genomic prediction of essential oil compounds in Atractylodes lancea for genomics-assisted breeding.
papers.journal: DNA research : an international journal for rapid publication of reports on genes and genomes
papers.summary: A chromosome-scale 4.79 Gb reference genome of Atractylodes lancea, a medicinal herb, was combined with GWAS and genomic prediction of essential oil compounds in 480 lines. Despite high heritability (h2 0.758-0.915), GWAS found only one weak locus, but genomic prediction exceeded 0.6 accuracy for all four compounds, demonstrating genomic selection's efficacy for medicinal plant breeding.

papers.title: Optical genome mapping improves structural variant detection and characterization in syndromic and neurogenetic disorders.
papers.summary: Optical genome mapping (OGM) was evaluated in 10 unsolved neurogenetic or syndromic cases. OGM confirmed all prior structural findings and added insights in five cases, including a novel candidate gene, refined breakpoints, complex rearrangements, and ring chromosomes 18, 20, and 22—requiring adjusted filters. OGM improved diagnostic yield in 6/10 cases, though not in hereditary neuropathy.

papers.title: MYBL2 promotes malignant phenotypes and M2-like macrophage polarization through CCL2 in non-small cell lung cancer.
papers.summary: MYBL2 is upregulated in non-small cell lung cancer, where silencing inhibited proliferation, migration, and invasion. MYBL2 directly binds the CCL2 promoter, enhancing CCL2 transcription; CCL2 supplementation rescued the effect of MYBL2 knockdown on macrophage polarization. The MYBL2-CCL2 axis promotes M2-like macrophage polarization, participating in NSCLC immune microenvironment remodeling.

papers.title: Tideglusib as a First-in-Class Chemical Probe for NatA: Identification, Mechanism, and Cellular Validation of an Allosteric, CoA-Dependent Inhibitor.
papers.summary: Tideglusib, a clinical-stage GSK-3β inhibitor, is the first small-molecule probe for N-terminal acetyltransferase A (NatA), which catalyzes 40-57% of eukaryotic Nα-acetylation. It binds allosterically, and CoA released during catalysis chemically modifies the drug into a reversible covalent adduct—a catalysis-dependent inhibition paradigm—with IC50 values of 0.68-1.8 μM and on-target acetylation suppression confirmed by proteomics.

papers.title: ZDHHC13 Is a Catalytically Deficient Protein S-Acyltransferase That Functions via a Noncanonical Mechanism.
papers.summary: ZDHHC13, an ankyrin-repeat S-acyltransferase with a noncanonical DQHC motif, is catalytically deficient: its catalytic cysteine shows minimal autoacylation, and a catalytically dead variant facilitated Huntingtin fragment S-acylation equally well in cells. ZDHHC13 resides in a high-molecular-weight complex, suggesting a scaffolding or accessory role, broadening understanding of noncanonical protein acyltransferase mechanisms.

papers.title: Development of m6A Readers for Enhanced Recognition In Vitro via Genetic Code Expansion.
papers.summary: Introducing noncanonical tryptophan derivatives at position W465 of the YTHDF1 YTH domain via genetic code expansion produced m6A readers with improved binding affinity and selectivity for m6A-modified RNAs. Energy decomposition analysis indicates substituent effects on dispersion forces in the van der Waals complex modulate binding, highlighting the CH-π interaction's role and a strategy for epitranscriptomic reader engineering.

papers.title: Live dynamics of induced cell-cell fusion between mitotic and interphasic cells.
papers.summary: Induced fusion of mitotic and interphase cells reveals mitosis as a dominant cytoplasmic state: mitotic cytoplasm drives interphase nuclei into aberrant mitosis with defective spindles and mitotic catastrophe, while high interphase:nucleus ratios force mitotic nuclei to exit, forming nuclei with defective nuclear import. These checkpoint overrides illuminate how competing cytoplasmic states integrate in syncytia.

papers.title: Maize Gametophytic factor loci Ga3 through Ga11 modify reproductive barriers.
papers.summary: Reassessing maize gametophytic factor loci Ga3-Ga11 reported between 1901 and modern times, this analysis concludes they are modifiers—rather than independent controllers—of the validated Ga1, Ga2, and Tcb1 barriers. Historical phenotypes fall into two categories, with candidate genes implicating pollen tube growth and RNA-directed DNA methylation pathways, framing reproductive barriers as shaped by epistatic interactions.

papers.title: Niche cell positioning drives functional heterogeneity in the Drosophila testis stem cell niche.
papers.summary: In the Drosophila testis stem cell niche, hub cells show significant architectural variation across strains and age. Hub cell position, but not origin, predicts function: stem cell-contacting cells produce more upd1, cycling cells more often contact the testis wall, and most cells anchor the niche via integrin adhesion—demonstrating functional heterogeneity within this classically 'simple' niche.

papers.title: Baseline cellular state shapes the molecular impact of mutant KRAS alleles in reconstituted pancreatic cancer cells.
papers.summary: Systematic transcriptomic, proteomic, and phosphoproteomic profiling of seven common KRAS mutants in isogenic KRAS-deficient pancreatic cancer cells found that baseline cellular state, not allele identity, predominantly drives molecular variation. No robust allele-specific programs emerged; interferon response and mitochondrial translation proteins were recurrently altered, with implications for interpreting putative allele-specific KRAS signaling dependencies.

papers.title: Mutations in the N-glycan branching enzyme MGAT1 promote invasiveness and EGF-stimulated proliferation and adhesion in neuroblastoma cells.
papers.summary: CRISPR mutation of MGAT1, the N-glycan branching enzyme, in neuroblastoma cells increased oligomannose-type N-glycans. Mutant cells showed strengthened cell-cell adhesion, greater invasiveness, enhanced EGF-stimulated EGFR phosphorylation and proliferation, and perpetual proliferation at high density—supporting a novel role for oligomannose N-glycans in neuroblastoma progression.

papers.title: N-acetylcysteine attenuates oxidative-stress-associated apoptosis and collagen deposition after rat hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion injury.
papers.summary: In a rat hindlimb ischemia-reperfusion model, oxidative DNA damage accumulation drove muscle apoptosis and collagen deposition underlying replantation contractures. N-acetylcysteine suppressed oxidative stress, apoptosis (Bax, caspase 3 versus Bcl2), and fibrosis-related CCN2 induction in myoblast cultures exposed to hydrogen peroxide, illuminating mechanisms of ischemia-reperfusion injury and potential countermeasures.

papers.title: Sex differences in social cognition: Insights from a sample enriched for social dysfunction.
papers.summary: In 212 adolescents and young adults spanning minimal to clinical social dysfunction, females outperformed males on perceptual theory of mind, social inferencing, and eye gaze perception, with most differences persisting after accounting for general cognition, age, and psychopathology. Results suggest females are more sensitive to subtle social signals, informing tailored treatments for social dysfunction.

papers.title: Modifications to a vegan artificial honey result in inhibitory activity against Mycobacterium abscessus.
papers.summary: A vegan 'honea' containing no bee-derived components—combining methylglyoxal, hydrogen peroxide, and key enzymes—was engineered and shown to inhibit and kill Mycobacterium abscessus in antimicrobial susceptibility testing. Both methylglyoxal and hydrogen peroxide contributed to the bactericidal effect, offering a synthetic, resource-independent alternative to manuka honey against this multidrug-resistant pathogen.

papers.title: 4-Phenylbutyric acid alleviates acrylamide-induced sexual behavioral deficits and testicular damage in male Wistar rats: modulation of ER-stress associated signaling.
papers.summary: Acrylamide exposure in male rats impaired sexual behavior, reduced testosterone and sperm count, and induced testicular oxidative and endoplasmic reticulum stress. 4-Phenylbutyric acid treatment improved sexual performance, restored hormone levels and histopathology, and reduced GRP78, CHOP, and caspase-12 expression, indicating ER-stress modulation as a protective mechanism against acrylamide reproductive toxicity.

papers.title: High TG/low HDL-C ratio-mimetic lipid stress drives diabetic atherosclerotic endothelial-macrophage dysfunction through glycocalyx disruption and CD36/ABCA1 imbalance.
papers.summary: A high triglyceride/low HDL cholesterol ratio-mimetic lipid stress model in human coronary endothelial cells and THP-1 macrophages revealed endothelial glycocalyx disruption (heparanase upregulation, syndecan-1 shedding), inflammatory activation, and a CD36/ABCA1 imbalance driving foam-cell formation. HDL rescue and heparanase or CD36 inhibition were protective, defining a glycocalyx-NF-κB-CD36/ABCA1 axis in diabetic atherosclerosis.

papers.title: Mechanistic insights into Mfd inhibition by pharmacophore-guided ligands using molecular and steered molecular dynamics simulations.
papers.summary: Using a pharmacophore model derived from the Mfd inhibitor NM102, researchers screened PubChem and food-derived phytochemicals for inhibitors of Mfd, the transcription repair coupling factor underlying bacterial mutagenesis and antibiotic persistence. Carpaine and a synthetic benzimidazole showed favorable docking to Mfd's ATP-binding region, stable complexes, and strong binding energies in molecular dynamics simulations.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of herbal medicines and bioactive compounds in rheumatoid arthritis: a comprehensive network pharmacology perspective.
papers.summary: This review applies network pharmacology—integrating bioinformatics, multi-omics, molecular docking, and validation—to explain how herbal compounds like quercetin, kaempferol, luteolin, triptolide, and berberine modulate NF-κB, PI3K/Akt, MAPK, JAK/STAT, and NLRP3 pathways in rheumatoid arthritis, affecting synoviocyte activation, macrophage polarization, and osteoclastogenesis, and bridging traditional medicine with multi-target drug discovery.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms of programmed cell death in aortic dissection and advances in clinical translation.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes how programmed cell death pathways—interacting with oxidative stress, mitochondrial dysfunction, immune infiltration, and matrix metalloproteinase activation—drive vascular smooth muscle cell loss and extracellular matrix degradation in aortic dissection. Clinical translation of cell-death-targeted precision therapies remains limited; current management still centers on imaging-based diagnosis, blood pressure control, and surgical repair.

papers.title: Genome-wide identification of the CCCH-type zinc finger gene family and functional characterization of PbrC3H45 in lignin biosynthesis of pear.
papers.summary: Genome-wide analysis identified 93 CCCH-type zinc finger genes in pear, with expansion driven mainly by whole-genome duplication. Co-expression across 206 sand pear accessions pinpointed PbrC3H45, and transformation assays confirmed it positively regulates lignin biosynthesis during stone cell formation—key determinants of pear fruit quality—providing targets for genetic improvement.

papers.title: GC(3)-biased, selection-shaped codon usage in WRKY, NAC and C2H2 transcription factor families of foxtail millet (Setaria italica).
papers.summary: Analysis of 418 coding sequences from WRKY, NAC, and C2H2 transcription factor families in foxtail millet revealed pronounced GC3 bias (>73%), G/C-ending optimal codons, and selection-dominated codon usage patterns. Neutrality plot slopes and correspondence analysis indicate natural selection shapes translational optimization, offering a framework for stress-tolerant crop improvement.

papers.title: Renal Cell Carcinoma: Histopathology, Molecular Features, and the Emerging Role of Organoid Models.
papers.summary: This review summarizes renal cell carcinoma's more than 20 histological subtypes within a molecularly informed classification, current tyrosine kinase inhibitor and immune checkpoint therapies with often transient responses, and the promise of patient-derived organoids for personalized drug-response testing—while noting gaps in culture condition standardization and tumor microenvironment recapitulation that limit clinical applicability.

papers.title: Clinical and functional characterization of 27 Chinese patients with 46, XY disorders of sex development caused by novel NR5A1 variants.
papers.journal: Sexual development : genetics, molecular biology, evolution, endocrinology, embryology, and pathology of sex determination and differentiation
papers.summary: Characterization of 27 novel NR5A1 variants in Chinese patients with 46,XY disorders of sex development showed a broad phenotypic spectrum without clear genotype-phenotype correlation. Functional assays in HEK293 cells revealed reduced protein levels for DNA-binding, A-box, and ligand-binding domain variants, variable transactivation deficits, and preserved nuclear localization, with greater functional tolerance in A-box and AF-2 domains.

papers.title: Biochemical characterization of a homocysteine S-methyltransferase from Leuconostoc suionicum.
papers.summary: The first homocysteine S-methyltransferase characterized from lactic acid bacteria, from Leuconostoc suionicum, is a monomeric ~32 kDa zinc-dependent enzyme with kcat/Km of 15.7 mM⁻¹s⁻¹ toward L-homocysteine, stable across 30-60°C and pH 5-9, preferring L- over D-homocysteine ~30-fold, accepting S-methylmethionine and SAM, and phylogenetically distinct from mammalian BHMT proteins.
